# Derived hook wiring (CLOUD-62)

One file per installable harness: the hook registrations
`batten generate hooks --harness <h>` emits for it.

**Goldens, not payloads.** The fixtures in the parent directory run the other
way — they are host payloads coming _in_, pinned so every host normalizes to one
envelope (CLOUD-44). These are what goes _out_: where each host reads its
registrations, and what to register there. Same hosts, opposite direction, so
they are kept apart rather than interleaved.

**What a diff here means.** These are regenerated by the emitter and compared
byte-for-byte in `tests/cli.rs`, so a change to a wiring row in
`crates/batten/src/hook.rs` shows up as a change to a file a reviewer can read.
That is the point: the rows are terse Rust data, and their consequence is a JSON
document a host will act on. Update a golden by re-running the emitter, never by
hand — a hand-edited golden is a second authority, which is the failure this
whole issue exists to remove.

Their facts — each host's config file and event spellings — come from the M1
harness capability matrix (CLOUD-209), the same survey the payload fixtures cite,
for the same stated reason: _"model memory of this space is badly stale … anything
re-derived without a fetch should be assumed wrong."_

`exit-code` has no file here. It is the neutral contract — envelope in, decision
as exit status out — not a host, so it has no config surface to register in, and
`generate hooks --harness exit-code` refuses with exit 1. `tests/cli.rs` asserts
that refusal, so the absence is covered rather than merely true.
